approach.method_basis: The Parent is a task-local genetic search over molecular graphs with a Bayesian screening layer in front of the oracle. It stores every molecule scored in the current task, breeds from the best of them by drawing parents from high-scoring score quantiles, and constructs each candidate either by connected-fragment crossover between two scored molecules, optionally followed by one mutation, or by a short chain of random atom and bond edits. Direct aromatic carbon-nitrogen exchange is switched off, and a sulfur rule refuses any offspring that introduces an unusual local sulfur environment its own generating parents did not already carry. Canonical identity checks drop invalid graphs and anything already proposed. Crucially, it does not send its newest offspring straight to the oracle. For every molecule it is allowed to propose it first breeds a surplus of sixteen fresh candidates, fits a Gaussian process to all accepted labels of the current task using integer-count Morgan fingerprints under a generalized Tanimoto kernel, and draws one joint sample of that posterior across the entire surplus field; the maximum of each draw, with already-chosen candidates masked out, becomes one proposal. Scored results then update the archive and a bounded population of the best molecules seen. In short, a graph genetic algorithm whose oracle budget is allocated by correlated Thompson sampling over a freshly bred candidate field.
approach.novelty: This Child changes exactly one thing: how wide that field is. The breeding rules, chemistry filters, surrogate, kernel, observation noise, sampling law and masking law are untouched; the search simply breeds sixty-four fresh offspring per proposal instead of sixteen, so each oracle call is chosen from six hundred and forty competing candidates instead of one hundred and sixty. Nothing is reused, deferred or harvested along the way: every extra candidate is bred from the current population by the same operators, under the same chemistry and identity filters, in the same batch. This lineage has run a sixteen-wide field in every node since the screening layer was introduced, and the Parent's own records show the ranking layer spreading its choices almost evenly over all one hundred and sixty positions, which is what you would expect if it is using the whole field it is given and has simply never been given more. The other same-Parent experiments in this round change what the surrogate believes - one blends a whole-molecule composition and property kernel into the covariance, another chooses the fingerprint radius by marginal likelihood - and a third removes a generator continuation step. Earlier siblings either deleted parts of the screening layer or widened the choice set with the wrong kind of candidate: one offered it last round's leftover proposals, another slipped unfinished intermediates of mutation chains into a pool of fixed size, and both lost score. This Child leaves the model and the generator laws alone and asks only whether more fresh competition per evaluation is worth its generation cost.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent is a complete matched panel: macro mean 0.596453 with population SD 0.033970, seed macros 0.643098, 0.563173 and 0.583088, and per-task means deco_hop 0.706940, drd2_docking 0.991017, median_2 0.222732, sitagliptin_mpo 0.604768 and zaleplon_mpo 0.456810 (n-1744a1494180). Reading its own fifteen stderr sessions, the limiting behaviour is how narrow the candidate field is that the posterior is allowed to rank. Across the panel the breeder produced 69,600 fresh pool members and exactly 4,350 of them were evaluated: one oracle call per sixteen fresh offspring. Of those 4,350 evaluated offspring only 648 (14.9 percent) beat their own best generating parent and only 255 (5.9 percent) improved the incumbent, so roughly nineteen of every twenty oracle calls buy no incumbent progress. Generation itself is not the constraint: 76,081 breeding attempts produced 69,600 admitted pool members (1.093 attempts each; 6,349 duplicates, 2 invalid graphs, 130 sulfur-gate rejections), the longest run of consecutive attempts for one pool member anywhere in seed 0 is five against inherited escalation thresholds at 40 and 80, and the inherited limit is 50,000 attempts per batch. Nor is the selector ignoring what it is given: the 4,350 selected pool indices are spread almost uniformly over positions 0 to 159 (455, 435, 439, 440, 452, 452, 433, 420, 415 and 409 across ten sixteen-wide bins; mean selected index 78.2; 48.9 percent at index 80 or later), 86.5 percent of choices differ from the posterior-mean argmax, and the chosen member sits at z = +1.054 inside its own pool's posterior-mean distribution while that pool's best mean sits at +1.735. Removing this allocator from this exact Parent costs 0.128183 (n-605c7a785b51), removing its sampled residual costs 0.116317 (n-f04cec6ab705), removing cross-candidate correlation costs 0.050545 (n-8df0bb3bbcfe), the same removal costs 0.124388 on the previous Parent (n-01b48dd09404) and adding the selector originally gained 0.0559 (n-fc2c108a5253). So the one component with the strongest measured contribution is being fed a sixteen-wide field per evaluation, a multiplier unchanged in every node of this lineage. The budget is also not saturated: all fifteen task/seed cells still improve their best-so-far between evaluation 200 and 300 (deco_hop seed 0 moves 0.6076 to 0.8561 after evaluation 250), so late evaluations still find new ground. Runtime leaves ample room: per-task wall is 24.3 to 106.7 seconds with 0.2 to 80.4 seconds of that in the oracle, and the three node totals are 214.8, 189.1 and 150.8 seconds, against a frozen 7,200-second task timeout and 40,500-second node timeout.
hypothesis: Quadruple only the fresh offspring pool target per announced batch member, from sixteen to sixty-four (160 to 640 candidates per announced batch of ten), so the unchanged accepted-only count-Tanimoto GP correlated Thompson selector takes its ten sequentially masked joint-draw maxima over a four-times larger field of fresh de novo offspring produced by the unchanged breeder, operators, continuation, crossover and finishing, sulfur gate and stable identity admission.

finding_summary.headline: Quadrupling the screened offspring field worked mechanically and bought nothing: endpoint mean fell 0.016, with no gain in selection quality
finding_summary.insights:
Candidate-set breadth is now measured on this lineage and it is not the lever. The pool multiplier had been 16 in every node since the screening layer was introduced, and the Parent's near-uniform use of all 160 positions had been read as evidence that the selector was field-limited. Quadrupling the field falsifies that reading: the selector spreads over 640 positions just as evenly, which means the uniformity was never a sign of hunger for more candidates, only of how flat the sampled posterior is across fresh offspring of one population. At a cost of four times the generation work per evaluation, the panel mean fell 0.016 and not one intermediate quantity moved enough to matter. Breadth under this selector is exhausted as a direction; the remaining headroom in this component is in the posterior and the acquisition rule, not in how many molecules they are shown.

The sharpest thing learned is the split between the field and the choice. The best candidate available in the pool improved measurably when the pool grew, yet the chosen candidate did not: the enlarged field's extra quality went into the tail of the sampled draw rather than into what was evaluated. With unit prior amplitude and a fixed noise SD of 0.05, a joint Thompson draw over a larger correlated field gets its maximum increasingly from residual extremes on uncertain members, and the diagnostics show exactly that drift. This makes a concrete, cheap next test available: hold the pool at 640 and shrink the effective residual scale, or take the posterior-mean argmax for a fraction of the ten slots, and see whether the improved pool maximum can be converted into improved selections. It also sharpens the reading of the earlier removal results, which showed the composite selector worth 0.128 on this Parent: that contribution is about having a posterior-ranked fresh field at all, not about its size.

The chemistry explains why extra screening could not help. The molecular review of this node finds the generator producing ring-rich frameworks finished with N-Cl, O-Cl, S-F and N-F bonds, free imines and thiocarbonyls, no trifluoromethyl group in 4,350 molecules, no formal charge and no assigned stereocentre, and on the flattest objective it grows oligomers to a mean of 43 heavy atoms and QED 0.19 rather than finding alternatives. A larger pool samples that same vocabulary more densely; it widens the degenerate tail along with the useful one, which is visible here as 181 near-trivial fragments emitted against the Parent's 105, and as the deco_hop seed-0 cell where mean emitted size reached 55.7 heavy atoms and 600 crossover products were rejected as invalid. Scaffold diversity, distinct scaffolds among the best fifty, and late-phase pairwise distance are all unchanged from the Parent, so the wider field did not produce collapse and did not produce discovery either; it produced more of the same chemistry.

Two things stay open. The deco_hop seed-0 contrast is dominated by the Parent's single late breakthrough at evaluation 281, which no Child in three rounds has reproduced, so the size of the loss is fragile even though its sign holds on two of three seeds; a trustworthy reading of that cell needs more seeds, not more analysis. And this result constrains one multiplier at one announced batch size. It does not establish that 16 is optimal, does not rule out that a much smaller field would do as well for a quarter of the compute, and says nothing about breadth under a different acquisition rule. The compute-efficiency question is now the interesting one in the other direction: if 640 buys nothing over 160, it is worth asking what 4 would cost.
finding_summary.results:
The enlarged field was built and used. Every one of the 435 batches across the complete fifteen-cell panel ranked exactly 640 fresh offspring, never truncated, at a modest generation cost of 1.147 breeding attempts per admitted member against the Parent's 1.093; the inherited escalation branches never fired and the longest struggle for a single pool member anywhere was nine attempts. The extra candidates genuinely competed: 73.3 percent of the 4,350 oracle calls went to members generated beyond position 160, the selection index distribution is nearly flat over all 640 positions, and the first 160 positions took 26.7 percent of the choices against the 25 percent expected if all members were interchangeable. That last number is the whole result in miniature: the later-generated members behaved exactly like the earlier ones. They beat their own generating parent at 0.152 and improved the incumbent at 0.063, against 0.153 and 0.067 for the members inside the Parent-sized prefix.

The screening-quality prediction failed. The registered test was that selected candidates should sit further above their own pool in posterior mean than the Parent's +1.054 standard deviations. They sat at +1.043, slightly lower, and fell in eight of fifteen cells, while the pool's own best available candidate did improve (+1.841 against +1.735). So the wider field did offer better candidates and the unchanged Thompson rule did not take them: it drew relatively more uncertain members (selected posterior SD 0.897 of the pool average, against 0.849 in the Parent), disagreed with the posterior-mean argmax in 92.8 percent of choices instead of 86.5, and picked members ranked on average 135th of 640 by posterior mean, 76.6 percent of them outside their pool's top ten. This is the registered failure mode for this intervention: four times more candidates means four times more chances for an extreme residual draw on an uncertain molecule, and that is what the enlarged field was spent on.

Downstream effects were real but tiny, and they went both ways. Parent-beating rose from 0.149 to 0.152 and incumbent improvement from 0.0586 to 0.0644, prediction error on emitted members fell slightly (batch MSE 0.0106 against 0.0112) and within-batch rank correlation rose from 0.526 to 0.546. Against that, the molecules actually evaluated were worse on average (mean offspring score 0.360 against 0.372) and larger (30.7 against 28.4 heavy atoms), with 181 emissions of five heavy atoms or fewer against 105.

The endpoint moved the wrong way. The complete matched panel mean fell 0.016060, from 0.596453 to 0.580393, against the registered requirement of at least +0.002; seed macros moved -0.044984, -0.012371 and +0.009174, six of fifteen cells improved, and the mean AUC fell from 0.4710 to 0.4555. Dispersion across seeds narrowed (population SD 0.0211 against 0.0340), which is not a substitute for the endpoint. Most of the panel loss is one cell: deco_hop seed 0 at -0.2459. The two runs were level there until evaluation 280 (Child 0.6088, Parent 0.6096), and then the Parent made its single rare late jump to 0.8561 while the Child finished at 0.6102. Excluding only that cell the panel would be close to flat. The largest gains were sitagliptin_mpo seed 2 at +0.0922 and zaleplon_mpo seed 0 at +0.0515. Compute behaved as predicted: non-oracle work rose about fourfold to a mean of 106 seconds per task, the worst task used 10.8 percent of its timeout and the worst node 2.9 percent, with no fallback, no truncation and every Cholesky succeeding at the smallest jitter.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic frameworks finished with N-Cl, O-Cl, S-F and N-F bonds, free imines and thiocarbonyls no chemist could isolate
molecular.overall_character: Across the five objectives the node proposed 4,350 molecules (870 per objective, 290 per seed, no repeat within a seed) and every one parsed. They are mid-sized and heavily cyclic: mean 24 to 43 heavy atoms, 3.0 to 5.0 rings and 1.9 to 3.8 aromatic rings per molecule, matching the digest ring_closure_rate of 0.944 to 0.976 and aromatic_atom_rate of 0.937 to 0.962. The skeletons are mostly recognisable medicinal chemistry: indole-2-carboxamides, pyrido-fused lactams, diarylmethane aminophenols, purine-like fused bicyclics. The decoration is not. The generator attaches halogens to heteroatoms as readily as to carbon: a nitrogen-, oxygen- or sulfur-bound halogen appears in 5.5 to 67.8 percent of proposals depending on objective, and in all thirty of the best molecules on one of them. It mints free imines, thioamides, thioketones, hydroxylamine and hydrazine ring links, hypochlorite esters and aryl thiols. It never once produced a trifluoromethyl group in 4,350 molecules, never produced a charged species, and the digest stereocentre_rate is 0.0 on all five objectives although RDKit finds at least one unassigned tetrahedral centre in 2,252 of the 4,350. Four-membered rings make up 2.5 to 14.9 percent of all rings. Between 2.6 and 5.5 percent of oracle calls went to fragments of five or fewer heavy atoms such as F, C=N and CSF, including one emitted at evaluation 298 of 300. The Parent pairing is complete (paired_complete true, matched seeds 0, 1 and 2) and all fifteen Parent trajectory files were read; Parent molecules are not citable under this brief, so Parent chemistry is reported only as aggregate counts computed over its 4,350 proposals. On that comparison the node drifted toward the same exotic decoration on every objective: heteroatom-bound halogens rose from 7.5, 15.6, 13.0, 1.7 and 11.7 percent of Parent proposals to 39.3, 67.8, 15.1, 5.5 and 10.1 percent, four-membered rings rose on all five, and tiny-fragment oracle calls rose on all five (Parent 1.0 to 3.8 percent).

per_task.generated_character: A single chemotype worked hard: 3-cyano-4-methoxy indole-2-carboxamides and their anilides, mean 24 heavy atoms, 3.0 rings and 2.2 aromatic rings, mean QED 0.51 and mean SA 3.6, so the frameworks themselves are ordinary and makeable. The best molecule, 0.5109, is Cc1c(C(=O)N(Cl)c2ccccc2)[nH]c2cc(C#N)c(CO)c(C)c12: an indole bearing a nitrile, a methyl, a hydroxymethyl and an N-chloro anilide. The chemotype is inherited directly from the initial population member COc1cc2[nH]c(C(=O)Nc3ccc(F)cc3)cc2c(OC)c1OC at 0.3051; 290 optimizer calls per seed added a nitrile, swapped methoxy for methyl or methylthio, and reached 0.5109. Walking the trajectory shows the mutation vocabulary plainly: at seed 0 evaluations 149 to 158 the amide carbonyl becomes a thioamide, then a free imine, then an N-hydroxy imine, while a benzylic methyl becomes CH2Cl and CH2Br and the indole is repeatedly dearomatised into quinoid tautomers.
liabilities: N-chloro amides (chloramides) in the single best molecule and in 21 of the top hundred; these are oxidants, not drugs
free primary ketimines C(=N)Ar in 35 of the top hundred, which hydrolyse on contact with water
thioamides and benzylic bromides along the search path, for example COc1c(C#N)cc2[nH]c(C(=S)Nc3ccccc3Cl)c(CBr)c2c1OC
48 of 870 proposals are five heavy atoms or fewer, including C1CSO1 and single-atom fragments scoring 0.0
missing_features: the fused five-six bridgehead-nitrogen bicyclic of the reference chemotype; the generator stays on an indole and never builds a bridgehead-nitrogen heteroaromatic
a tertiary acetamide side chain; only 2 percent of proposals carry a tertiary amine and the top hundred carry none
a clean heavy-atom and heteroatom budget; adding Cl or Br as decoration spends atoms a formula-matching term cannot use
aryl substituents installed as whole groups; changes arrive one atom at a time, so para-substituted phenyl motifs are never placed in a single move
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score rises with the fused bicyclic aromatic core plus a nitrile and an aryl amide: the top thirty average 2.83 aromatic rings and QED 0.60, the bottom thirty average 0.07 rings and score exactly 0.0. Above 0.47 the gradient is nearly flat and is being paid in decoration, not structure. COc1c(SC)c(C#N)cc2[nH]c(C(=O)Nc3ccccc3)c(C)c12, a clean N-H anilide, scores 0.4823, and its N-chloro analogue scores 0.4868: the chloramide buys 0.0045. Free imines do the same, COc1c(C)c(C#N)cc2[nH]c(C(=N)c3ccccc3)c(CO)c12 at 0.4834.

per_task.generated_character: The least chemical set in the node. Mean 43 heavy atoms, mean molecular weight 685, mean 5.0 rings, mean QED 0.19 and 56 percent of proposals above SA 4.5. The best molecule, 0.6104, is CC=CC(=CC)Cc1nc(F)nn1Cc1nc(C(=O)Oc2nc(N(Cl)C(=O)N(C=O)C(=O)N(C=O)SF)ncc2Br)ncc1Br: two bromopyrimidines joined through a triazole, an aryl ester of a hydroxypyrimidine, a chain of three formamides, an N-chloro urea and a terminal S-F bond. Its near-equal partner CCC=COn1nc2c3c1CCn2c(=O)n(-n1c(=O)n(CF)c(=O)c2c(C)n(-c4cc5c(cc4OCl)CCCCC5=S)nc21)c3=O carries an aryl hypochlorite O-Cl, a thioketone and an enol ether. All thirty of the best molecules carry at least one heteroatom-bound halogen; the top hundred contain 38 O-Cl, 37 S-F, 20 N-Cl and 36 aldehydes. The same aggregate over the Parent top hundred contains zero O-Cl, zero S-F and zero N-Cl.
liabilities: aryl hypochlorite esters O-Cl in 38 of the top hundred, which are oxidants of explosive grade
sulfenyl fluoride S-F in 37 of the top hundred and N-chloro ureas in 20
thioketones C=S on saturated carbocycles, which oligomerise rather than sit on a shelf
mean QED 0.19 and 56 percent of proposals above SA 4.5: a chemist would reject the whole top set
39 of 870 proposals are five heavy atoms or fewer and score the 0.5 floor, for example CC=O and CSF
missing_features: a compact decorated core rather than a grown oligomer; these molecules exceed 40 heavy atoms where the Parent reached a higher score near 30
stable halogen placement on carbon; the reward is being reached with halogen on oxygen, nitrogen and sulfur instead
hydrogen-bond donors: the top thirty average zero donors, so any donor-dependent recognition term is unreachable
ring systems of ordinary size; 14.9 percent of all rings here are four-membered and 1.9 percent are nine-membered
a linker motif built as one unit; linkers here are assembled atom by atom into formamide and urea chains
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The floor is 0.5 and every fragment sits on it: CC=O, CSF and Br all score exactly 0.5, as does the whole bottom thirty. The initial population member CCOC(=O)c1ccc(O)c(-n2cc3c(c2-c2ccccc2)c(=O)n(C)c(=O)n3C)c1, an ordinary drug-like molecule, already scores 0.5484, so 290 optimizer calls per seed bought at most +0.062 over it. Above 0.60 the gradient is flat and the optimizer pays for it by growing: top thirty 40 heavy atoms, whole set 43, while the Parent top thirty averaged 30.5 heavy atoms at a higher score. The final molecules repeat this, for example O=C(OCCl)c1cc(C(=NBr)c2c3cc(c(OBr)c(OCl)cc(Br)n2Cl)CCS3)c(O)nc1OCCl at 0.5933.

per_task.generated_character: The most convincing chemistry in the node, and the only objective whose top thirty contains no heteroatom-bound halogen. The best molecule, 0.9925, is Cc1cc(Br)cc(C(C)CCN2CC3CC2N3c2ccc(F)c(N)c2)c1S: a 2,5-diazabicyclo[2.2.1]heptane with an N-aryl group on one nitrogen and a propyl tether to a bromotoluene, a real medicinal-chemistry motif. All thirty best molecules carry a basic amine, averaging 3.3 per molecule; 97 of the top hundred carry a primary amine and 85 a secondary amine. Mean 31 heavy atoms, 3.6 rings, 1.9 aromatic rings, mean logP 5.0 and mean QED 0.37. The later seed-2 molecules are flatter diarylmethane aminophenols with aminoalkyl chains, for example CCNCC12CCOc3c1ccc(c3F)C2c1cc(F)c(N)c(CCCN)c1 at 0.9782.
liabilities: aryl thiols on the two best molecules, which oxidise to disulfides and are classic assay interferers
a 2-chloroethylamine nitrogen mustard in COc1cc(Br)cc(C2CC=C(C(CNCCCl)c3cccc(O)c3)CN2)c1N at 0.9902, an alkylating liability
O-S bonds in late emissions such as CNCCc1ccc(Cc2cc(CF)c(N)cc2O)c(F)c1OSC
30 of 870 proposals are five heavy atoms or fewer, including C=N emitted at evaluation 298 of 300
aniline-rich frameworks carrying several free primary amines, a metabolic and toxicological liability
missing_features: a cyclic basic amine of the aryl-piperazine or aryl-piperidine class; piperazine appears in about 1 percent of proposals and effectively none of the top hundred
an amide or sulfonamide linkage: the top hundred contain zero of each, so the high-scoring set is amine and ether only
aromatic ring count above two in the high-scoring set, which averages exactly 2.0 aromatic rings
controlled lipophilicity; the set averages logP 5.0 with no polar counterweight
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The gradient is almost entirely basic nitrogen plus an aromatic ring pair. The bottom thirty average 0.33 basic nitrogens, 0.8 rings and score 0.005; the top thirty average 3.3 basic nitrogens, 3.5 rings and score 0.977. Progress is abrupt: seed 0 best-so-far moves 0.283 at evaluation 100 to 0.857 at 200 to 0.992 at 300, consistent with the score being carried by acquiring one protonatable amine on an aryl framework. Once that is present further change is noise, and the optimizer still emits C=N, a two-atom fragment scoring 0.0075, at evaluation 298 of 300.

per_task.generated_character: The most drug-like set in the node and the most collapsed. The best molecule, 0.2433, is CCCc1ccccc1N1CC(=O)N(C)CCc2c(c(=O)[nH]c3ccc(OCC)cc23)N1C: an ethoxy-quinolinone fused to a seven-membered piperazinone-like lactam, N-aryl substituted with 2-propylphenyl. Mean 30 heavy atoms, 4.3 rings, mean QED 0.62, and 79 percent of proposals carry an amide; 93 of the top hundred carry an amide and 100 a pyridine-type aromatic nitrogen. The top of the search is one scaffold permuted at a single atom: the digest twelve best differ only in the atom linking the aryl group to the lactam nitrogen, N in the best, O-N in CCCc1ccccc1ON1CC(=O)N(C)CCc2c(c(=O)[nH]c3ccc(OCC)cc23)N1C at 0.2414, N-N at 0.2381 and C at 0.2381, with N-F substitution at 0.2365.
liabilities: aryl hydroxylamine O-N and hydrazine N-N linkages used as scaffold variations, both unstable and mutagenicity-flagged
N-fluoro amines in 12 of the top hundred, for example CCCc1ccccc1N1CC(=O)N(C)CCc2c(c(=O)[nH]c3ccc(OCC)cc23)N1F
16 percent of rings in this set are seven-membered and 8.4 percent are nine-membered, which strains synthesis
23 of 870 proposals are five heavy atoms or fewer, including C#C and single-carbon fragments scoring 0.0
missing_features: a second distinct chemotype at the top; the high-scoring region is one scaffold with one atom varied
ring replacement rather than atom replacement, so no alternative fused bicyclic is ever tested at high score
a carboxylic acid or sulfonamide polar group: neither appears anywhere in the top hundred
halogen on carbon as a tuning handle; this set is nearly halogen-free at a digest halogen_rate of 0.134, and the halogens that do appear arrive on nitrogen
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The whole usable range is narrow, best 0.2433 against a median of 0.194 and a best initial molecule of 0.1678, and the gradient rewards a fused aromatic lactam carrying an alkoxy group plus one basic nitrogen: the top thirty average 3.0 aromatic rings, 2.0 basic nitrogens and QED 0.59, the bottom thirty average 0.4 rings and score 0.025. Within the top thirty the spread is 0.008 across twelve different linking atoms, so the gradient has stopped distinguishing chemistry and is distinguishing single atom identities.

per_task.generated_character: Fluorine-saturated fused heterocycles that are not isolable compounds. The best molecule, 0.7123, is CN=c1c2c3n(C=CC(C=O)=CF)c(c2n(F)c(=N)n1C)C(F)(CF)C=CO3: a purine-like tricycle carrying two exocyclic ketimines, an N-fluoro ring nitrogen, a fluoromethyl group, an enol ether and a pendant fluoro-enal. Every one of the thirty best molecules sits above SA 4.5, mean SA 5.82, and only one of thirty carries a basic amine, against 80 percent in the Parent top thirty. 82 of the top hundred carry an N-F bond and 41 a vinyl fluoride. Mean 26 heavy atoms, 3.1 rings, mean QED 0.58 over the whole set but 0.42 over the top thirty.
liabilities: N-fluoro amines and N-fluoro amides in 82 of the top hundred, which are fluorinating reagents rather than drug molecules
two exocyclic ketimines per molecule in the best series, which hydrolyse immediately
aldehydes in 43 of the top hundred, reactive and metabolically unstable
100 percent of the top thirty above SA 4.5, mean 5.82, the least makeable set in the node
41 of 870 proposals are five heavy atoms or fewer, including F, FF and O at score 0.0
missing_features: a trifluoromethyl group: not one appears in the 870 proposals here, nor in any of the node 4,350 molecules
fluorine placed on aromatic carbon as a stable handle, rather than on ring nitrogen
a basic primary amine on a saturated carbon, present in only 1 of the 30 best molecules

per_task.score_gradient_reading: The gradient tracks fluorine count on a nitrogen-rich fused core: the bottom thirty are fragments like F, FF and O at exactly 0.0, the whole set averages 2.0 halogens and the top thirty average 3.7. It is also a cliff, not a slope. CN=c1c2c3n(C=CC(C=O)=CF)c(c2n(F)c(=N)n1C)C(F)(CF)C=CO3 scores 0.7123 while the single-atom variant CN=c1c2c3n(C=CC(C=O)=CF)c(c2n(F)c(=N)n1C)C(N)(F)C=CO3, which only replaces a fluoromethyl with an amine, scores 0.001 and was still emitted at evaluation 299 of 300. A sibling that swaps one ring N-F for N-CH2F, CN=c1c2c3n(C=CC(C=O)=CF)c(c2n(CF)c(=N)n1C)C(F)(S)C=CO3, holds 0.5867.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A halogen bonded to N, O or S appears in 5.5 to 67.8 percent of the proposals depending on the objective, in all thirty of the best molecules on one of them, and as 38 O-Cl, 37 S-F and 20 N-Cl instances inside a single hundred-molecule high-scoring set. Its own best molecules on two other objectives reach the top of their range with the halogen on carbon or with no halogen at all.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator attaches halogens to nitrogen, oxygen and sulfur as freely as to carbon, so its highest-scoring molecules are decorated with groups that are oxidants rather than substituents.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The mutation and crossover operators need a valence-context rule, enforced at the admission point that already audits sulfur, permitting halogen attachment only on carbon unless the parent already carried that bond. This is a property of the operator vocabulary and costs nothing on carbon.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Not one trifluoromethyl group appears in the node 4,350 molecules, although fluorine-rich scoring is clearly being chased: one high-scoring set averages 3.7 halogens per molecule and supplies them as 82 N-F bonds and 41 vinyl fluorides per hundred molecules. The same high-scoring sets contain zero sulfonamides and zero carboxylic acids, and amide content falls to zero in one of them.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator has no multi-atom functional-group vocabulary; it adds or swaps one atom at a time and never assembles a complete group in a single move.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The breeder needs a small library of intact substituents (trihalomethyl, sulfonamide, carboxylate, alkoxyaryl, cyclic amine) placed as single atomic moves, so a group whose value is collective rather than per-atom becomes reachable in one mutation instead of three individually unrewarded ones.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Zero of 4,350 molecules carry a formal charge and the digest stereocentre_rate is 0.0 on all five proposal sets, while RDKit finds at least one unassigned tetrahedral centre in 2,252 of those same 4,350 molecules. Half the output therefore has a three-dimensional identity the graph never commits to.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator emits only flat, uncharged graphs: no formal charge and no specified configuration anywhere in its output.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The representation needs stereochemical assignment as a mutable attribute and ionisable groups in its vocabulary. Until both exist, any scoring surface that separates enantiomers or depends on a salt bridge is invisible to the search however large the candidate pool becomes.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Between 2.6 and 5.5 percent of proposals are molecules of five or fewer heavy atoms (F, O, FF, C#C, C=N, CC=O, CSF), against 1.0 to 3.8 percent for the Parent on the matched sets. One two-heavy-atom fragment was emitted at evaluation 298 of 300 and another at 299 of 300, where the incumbent was still improving.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator spends oracle calls on degenerate fragments it cannot improve, and did so more than its Parent on every one of the five proposal sets.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Admission needs a minimum heavy-atom floor, or the ranker needs fragment size in its representation. A fourfold larger candidate field widens the degenerate tail as much as the useful one, so the filter belongs in the generator rather than in the ranker.

transferable_gaps.evidence: On one proposal set the twelve best molecules differ only in the identity of the one atom linking an aryl group to a lactam nitrogen (N, O-N, N-N, C, N-F, N-CH3-N) across a span of 0.008 in score. On another, a fifty-molecule high-scoring region contained only four distinct Murcko scaffolds, with thirty-six copies of one of them.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator cannot leave a chemotype once it reaches one; its late exploitation is single-atom permutation of a single scaffold rather than scaffold change.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The operator set needs a ring-replacement or scaffold-hop move that exchanges a whole ring system while preserving substituent positions. Atom-identity mutation alone makes late search a local relabelling of one graph, which a larger candidate pool amplifies rather than cures.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Free primary ketimines appear in 35 of one hundred-molecule high-scoring set and twice per molecule in another set's best series; thioketones on saturated carbocycles, thioamides, aryl hypochlorite esters, hydroxylamine and hydrazine ring links, aryl thiols, O-S bonds and a 2-chloroethylamine mustard all occur in molecules at or near the top of their range.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator freely mints functional groups that cannot be isolated, and carries no stability filter beyond its single existing sulfur rule.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A reactive-group rejection list applied at the admission gate that already audits sulfur would remove these without touching the ranker, the batching or the operators. The point is that nothing in the current pipeline expresses chemical stability at all.

transferable_gaps.evidence: On the proposal set whose gradient plateaued, molecules averaged 43 heavy atoms, molecular weight 685, QED 0.19 and 56 percent above SA 4.5, and the thirty best averaged 40 heavy atoms with zero hydrogen-bond donors, while the Parent thirty best on the matched set averaged 30.5 heavy atoms at a higher score. Four-membered rings rose from 2.5 to 9.1 percent of all rings in the Parent sets to 9.1 to 14.9 percent here.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator grows molecules when the score surface goes flat, with no size or property brake.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The breeder needs a size or ligand-efficiency brake that engages when the incumbent is not advancing, so a flat region yields structural alternatives of comparable size rather than larger copies of the incumbent. Enlarging the candidate pool does not supply this, because every member inherits the same growth bias.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

retained_mechanisms: Accepted-only task-local chronological archive, greedy 64-member survivor population and score-quantile parent sampling at edges [0.10, 0.25, 0.50] with weights [0.60, 0.30, 0.10].

Connected-fragment crossover at probability 0.45 with the >40-attempt halving, optional finishing mutation at 0.35, and ordinary one-to-three-step mutation continuation over seven atom/bond/ring families with the //80 escalation; direct aromatic C/N exchange disabled.

Stable canonical isomeric identity admission with emitted/initial and pool-local duplicate rejection, max_atoms 120, and the inherited 5,000-attempts-per-member (50,000 per batch) limit with its exhaustion raise and partial-pool break.
Source-relative sulfur introduction gate taking the per-signature maximum over the actually scored generating parents at pool admission.

Chirality-aware 2048-bin folded Morgan count features at radius 2 with the dot-product generalized Tanimoto covariance, archive mean/population-SD normalization with floor 0.001, observation noise SD 0.05 and the jitter ladder from 1e-8.

Correlated joint-posterior Thompson batch allocation over the fresh pool with sequential availability masking, first-index ties, the generation-order fallback, prediction feedback and next-fit probes.

CHANGED: the fresh offspring pool target per announced batch member, 16 to 64, so the unchanged selector ranks 640 candidates per batch of ten instead of 160. No new mechanism is added and none is removed; the node's mechanism count is unchanged from the Parent.
